report.headline: Tennessee grinds Auburn down with Bishop and a capped passing game
report.openingParagraph: Tennessee 24, Auburn 14 at Neyland. The market had Tennessee by 6 and the model had Tennessee by 5.1 with a 63 percent win probability, so the side was never the interesting part. The interesting part was how it happened, and it happened on the ground and in front of the safeties, exactly where the unit edges pointed.

sections.title: The run game decided it
paragraphs: DeSean Bishop carried 33 times for 216 yards and 3 touchdowns. Tennessee ranks No. 16 of 138 in line yards at 3.54 and runs at a 40 percent pass rate, and Auburn's defense sat No. 38 in line yards at 2.57 and No. 36 in rush success allowed. The volume answer beat the efficiency answer.
Tennessee also led the country's near-elite tier inside the 40, at 5.31 points per trip, No. 5 of 138. Short fields turned into touchdowns instead of kicks.

sections.title: The lid stayed on both quarterbacks
paragraphs: Tennessee is No. 1 of 138 at limiting explosive passes at 1.10, and Auburn's 1.58 pass explosiveness never got loose. Byrum Brown went 22 of 33 for 159 yards with 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions, and he added 19 carries for 107 yards and a score. Dejuan Lane took one of those picks 32 yards and finished with 9 tackles, 2.5 for loss and 2 sacks.

Tennessee did not push the ball either. George MacIntyre went 8 of 10 for 86 yards, and Faizon Brandon's line was 3 of 8 for 0 yards with an interception and 4 carries for minus 9. Tennessee entered No. 120 in pass explosiveness. Both passing games drove the long way, which is why the model's 46 total sat so far under the posted 54.5.

sections.title: Draft-lens notes
paragraphs: Mike Matthews finished with 4 catches for 57 yards on a 24-point day, in line with an 11 percent usage share. Da'Shawn Womack had his best stat line of the season, 5 tackles, 3 for loss and 2 sacks, and Elijah Melendez added 9 tackles, 2 for loss, a sack and a pass breakup. Auburn's front won snaps. Tennessee's 33 carries to Bishop still won the game.

report.oneLineForCard: Tennessee 24, Auburn 14: Bishop ran 33 times for 216 yards while both passing games stayed capped.
